packageRules.description: The platform check runs rancher-platform's Ansible on the setup-python interpreter, and ansible-core 2.21 does not run on Python 3.15 (AttributeError: module 'dataclasses' has no attribute '_is_type'). Hold platform.yaml below 3.15 until rancher-platform's ansible/requirements-ci.txt moves to ansible-core 2.22 and its own e2e hold is lifted.

Rancher is the one pin of the provider stack. The Turtles release it bundles (its build.yaml turtlesVersion) and that release's provider catalogue (config-prime.yaml) fix Turtles, core CAPI, CAPD, CAPA and CAPRKE2, so a Rancher update PR carries all of them: the Provider sync workflow runs scripts/sync-providers.py on it and commits the rewritten pins. The required platform check deploys that Rancher with those providers, provisions the Docker RKE2 example through Fleet, CAPI and CAPRKE2, and waits for Turtles to import it into Rancher, so updates automerge on that check after the preset's age gates. CAPA is only installed and started: nothing exercises AWS.
Rancher majors wait for a person. The rule above would otherwise automerge them over the preset's manual major rule.
prBodyNotes: **Why this waits for you:** a major release in the Rancher/Turtles provider stack can drop APIs or change the upgrade path. The platform check proves a fresh install, not an upgrade of running clusters; read the release notes and docs/migration.md before merging.

packageRules.description: Turtles, core CAPI, CAPD, CAPA and CAPRKE2 follow the Rancher pin (see the rule above), never their own releases: a standalone bump installs providers the bundled Turtles was not tested with, and validate rejects pins that differ from its catalogue. The markers stay so the dashboard still lists the versions.
Review RKE2, the kind node image and the AWS CCM together, by hand.
A new minor needs new immutable templates and a CCM migration.
